item.title: EFAWDet: Efficient Frequency-Role Assigned Wavelet-State-Space Fusion for RGB–Infrared Object Detection
item.description: Red, green, and blue (RGB)–infrared (IR) object detection leverages complementary visible texture and thermal cues to improve robustness under challenging conditions. However, existing feature-level fusion methods lack explicit frequency-role assignment: low-frequency semantic structures and high-frequency localization details are indiscriminately processed, squandering computation on redundant responses while suppressing the edge cues essential for precise localization. Moreover, global modeling operators such as Transformers and state-space models are uniformly applied to all frequency components, further degrading small-object boundaries. To address these issues, we propose a lightweight frequency-decoupled framework, namely efficient RGB-infrared detector (EFAWDet) that explicitly allocates distinct frequency bands to distinct detection functions. In EFAWDet, a multigroup wavelet fusion (MGWF) module decomposes dual-modal features and routes compact low-frequency components, which encode stable target-body semantics, to grouped cross-modal fusion. Then, a multigroup noncausal state-space duality (NC-SSD) performs noncausal global interaction confined within these reduced-resolution channel groups. Significantly, the separated RGB/IR high-frequency subbands are first adaptively fused through lightweight attention, then cached and reintroduced at the enhanced detection head (EDH) through inverse wavelet reconstruction as delayed localization compensation. This “low-frequency global modeling, high-frequency delayed compensation” strategy aligns the spectral properties of IR imagery with the frequency bias of state-space modeling, simultaneously reducing redundancy and preserving fine-grained localization cues. Extensive experiments on M3FD, LLVIP, forward-looking infrared (FLIR)-aligned, and DroneVehicle demonstrate state-of-the-art performance. EFAWDet-nano achieves 87.6% mAP50 and 58.7% mean average precision (mAP) on M3FD with only 2.5 M parameters and 16.5 GFLOPs (209.0 FPS), yielding a 99.1% reduction in parameter count compared to the YOLOv8-based FusionMamba while sacrificing merely 0.1 percentage point in mAP. The source code will be available at https://github.com/chenHeaven/EFAWDet
item.authors: Zhenghua Huang;Haiwen Chen;Qian Li;Yaozong Zhang;Chunhua Deng;Xin Xu;

item.title: Bidirectional Entity Coupling Alignment for Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Image–Text Retrieval
item.description: Due to the homogeneous backgrounds and cluttered layouts of remote sensing (RS) imagery, fine-grained local entities are indispensable for preventing cross-modal semantic mismatch. However, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods based on contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) encapsulate scenes into holistic global representations, diluting these critical local cues. To address this, we propose the bidirectional entity-level alignment network (BEAN), a unified fine-grained entity alignment paradigm. First, to avoid the semantic ambiguity of conventional extraction mechanisms, we introduce a symmetric visual and textual entity construction paradigm comprising a visual entity bank constructor (VEBC) and a noun-to-token index constructor (NTIC). Specifically, VEBC constructs a visual entity bank via layerwise extraction, while NTIC performs index-guided extraction of textual entity embeddings, jointly delivering semantically discriminative cross-modal entity pairs. Second, to counteract the submersion of local entities within global embeddings, we design the cross-modal entity-bidirectional adapter (CEBA). It drives bidirectional cross-attention between the global feature stream and localized entity tokens. This mutually enriches isolated entities with holistic scene context, while simultaneously reinjecting fine-grained entity cues back into the global representations, effectively reversing the dilution process. Third, to overcome the absence of explicit entity-level supervision in traditional global contrastive objectives, we propose the fine-grained entity contrastive loss, a sample-level formulation that provides direct supervision for explicit entity alignment without requiring manual positive–negative pair annotation. Experiments on RSITMD, RSICD, and UCM-Captions datasets demonstrate that BEAN achieves leading mR scores of 50.74%, 34.67%, and 60.56%, respectively, consistently outperforming both PEFT-based methods and the fully fine-tuned CLIP baseline across all three benchmarks. The code is available at https://github.com/JasonGravity/BEAN
item.authors: Mengru Ma;Jiaxu Guo;Wenping Ma;Licheng Jiao;Yuting Yang;Xu Liu;Lingling Li;Fang Liu;

item.title: SSLANet: A Frequency–Spatial Visual System for Efficient Hyperspectral Image Classification
item.description: Hyperspectral image classification requires a compact representation that can jointly capture discriminative spectral cues, local spatial structures, and efficient inference behavior under limited annotations. Existing CNN-based methods provide effective local pattern extraction but are less capable of modeling long-range spectral dependencies. Transformer-based models improve global interaction at the cost of considerable computational overhead, whereas recent state-space models usually formulate hyperspectral data as spatial–spectral sequences and still leave transform-domain spectral variations insufficiently explored. To address these limitations, we propose a spectral–spatial learning adaptive network (SSLANet), an efficient frequency–spatial learning network for hyperspectral image classification. The core component is a residual frequency–spatial layer that integrates an adaptive spectral block (ASB) and an interactive convolution block (ICB). ASB performs learnable complex-valued spectral modulation together with input-dependent frequency-energy selection to enhance material-sensitive spectral responses, while ICB propagates the filtered features into local neighborhoods through multiplicative spatial–channel interaction. This design differs from fixed transform-domain preprocessing in that the frequency response is conditioned on the current input feature distribution through a soft mask and an effective transfer function in the latent frequency domain. Extensive experiments on three public hyperspectral benchmarks demonstrate that SSLANet achieves competitive classification accuracy with favorable computational efficiency. The source code is available at https://github.com/NELUJA86/SSLANet
item.authors: Xiaofei Yang;Ruiying Zhang;Weijia Cao;Jiangtao Peng;Yifang Ban;Yicong Zhou;

item.title: Difference Approximation Network With Semantic Alignment for Remote Sensing Change Captioning
item.description: Remote sensing change captioning (RSCC) plays an important role in advancing remote sensing spatiotemporal understanding with vision-language generation. However, due to the temporal evolution of geospatial patterns, bitemporal images are susceptible to the influence of lighting conditions and seasonal effects. Existing methods fail to effectively utilize the cross-sample difference information and perform explicit multimodal alignment of key changes, which often results in inaccurate descriptions of changes in key objects and their relationships. To address these issues, the article proposes a novel difference approximation network with semantic alignment (DANSA) for RSCC. Specifically, a cross-temporal feature transform (CFT) is introduced to interact with feature representations extracted from the contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) model. Then, to learn a reliable difference representation, a difference memory approximation (DMA) is designed to enhance the difference representation of the current scene by activating difference information from training samples. Furthermore, considering that pretrained language embedding models can serve as a powerful supervisory signal, a change semantic alignment (CSA) is constructed to achieve fine-grained alignment between visual and textual features. In this way, DANSA generates comprehensive scene change captions that accurately depict objects and relationships across time. Extensive experiments and analyses conducted on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that DANSA achieves competitive performance with fewer training parameters. The code will be available at https://github.com/zcsisiyao/DANSA
item.authors: Cheng Zhang;Zhongle Ren;Biao Hou;Shijie Liu;Changhui Xu;Weibin Li;Licheng Jiao;

item.title: How Many Independent Samples Does a Satellite Image Contain? Generalization Bounds for Spatially Dependent Data
item.description: Machine learning classifiers for remote sensing imagery are typically evaluated as though every pixel were an independent sample. Spatial autocorrelation violates this assumption, since neighboring pixels carry redundant information which inflates sample sizes. How many independent samples does a satellite image actually contain? For an $n \times n$ image whose spatial correlation persists over a range of $r$ pixels, the effective sample size is $\Theta (n^{2}/r^{2})$ , not $n^{2}$ . We prove this as a finite-sample upper bound for classifiers on spatially correlated data, and show via a matching lower bound that the rate is tight, and no algorithm can do better. We extend the results to images with directional correlation and spatially varying correlation structure. Our result justifies spatial cross-validation since block holdout with separation proportional to the correlation range achieves optimal generalization guarantees, while random holdout can underestimate confidence interval widths by a factor proportional to $r$ . We validate the theory on synthetic data and satellite image tiles from three sensors (Landsat 8, Sentinel-2, and Sentinel-1).
item.authors: Robin Young;

item.title: MAPLE: Modality-Adaptive Prior-Guided Learning With Language-Conditioned Spatial Adaptation for Multimodal Remote Sensing Segmentation
item.description: Multimodal remote sensing segmentation benefits from complementary information across heterogeneous data sources, yet effectively leveraging such information while preserving the generalization ability of pretrained models remains challenging. In this article, we propose modality-adaptive prior-guided learning (MAPLE), a unified framework that adapts a frozen foundation backbone for multimodal learning via lightweight modality-aware mechanisms and language-guided priors. By introducing adaptive feature modulation and semantic guidance, the proposed approach effectively mitigates modality discrepancies and improves spatial prediction consistency. In addition, an adaptive reweighting strategy is employed to address class imbalance and enhance the learning of underrepresented categories. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks demonstrate that MAPLE achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with the smallest trainable footprint among the compared methods, while a comprehensive efficiency analysis of total parameters, floating-point operations (FLOPs), inference latency, and memory consumption further confirms a favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-off. The source code is available at https://github.com/shiroSamaNanoda/MAPLE.git
item.authors: Qiao Sun;Zechao Hu;Lin Chen;Zerui Xiao;Shukan Liu;Hui Yang;Xianzhang Chen;

item.title: Reliability-Aware Spatiotemporal Consistency Regulation for Satellite Video Tracking
item.description: The satellite video single object tracking (SVSOT) remains challenging because low image quality and cluttered backgrounds yield unreliable target evidence. Although recent trackers have improved robustness by enhancing feature representations and cross-frame interactions, they lack regulation of the reliability of evidence used for recursive feature updates. As single object tracking (SOT) can be seen as a recursive process, once unreliable evidence is absorbed into the target state, it may bias subsequent associations, accumulate spatiotemporal inconsistency, and eventually cause tracking drift or failure. To tackle these issues, we propose SCRTrack, a spatiotemporal consistency regulation framework that regulates the formation of target evidence and its propagation and maintenance across frames. Specifically, a multilayer feature formation (MFF) module is proposed to inject shallow structural details into deep semantic representations, enhancing spatial discriminability while suppressing clutter-induced interference. A reliability-guided context propagation (RCP) module is further designed to estimate interframe correspondence reliability and uses it to modulate temporal state updates, reducing the impact of ambiguous associations on state evolution. In addition, a motion consistency preservation (MCP) mechanism is introduced to monitor motion-consistent response displacements under occlusion and similar-object interference, maintaining target identity when appearance-based evidence becomes unreliable. Extensive experiments on SatSOT, SV248S, and OOTB demonstrate that SCRTrack achieves the state-of-the-art performance and exhibits strong robustness across challenging satellite tracking scenarios.
item.authors: Xiaowen Zhang;Haijiang Sun;Hanqing Sun;Hongliang Chang;Xilai Wei;Chao Ma;

item.title: HydroDrone: A Circular External-Looking UAV-SAR Campaign for Short-Term Temporal Decorrelation Characterization
item.description: This article presents the HydroDrone campaign, a dedicated uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-based synthetic aperture radar (SAR) experiment designed to characterize short-term temporal decorrelation over vegetated scenes. The system employs a C-band frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar mounted on a multirotor UAV, performing repeated circular external-looking acquisitions over a chosen test site. This configuration enables the generation of dense interferometric stacks with temporal baselines ranging from tens of seconds to several hours. This work derives the specific mathematical framework for the computation of along-track wavenumbers and azimuth resolution in circular external-looking geometries, highlighting the fundamental differences with respect to standard linear trajectories. To compensate for residual trajectory errors arising from navigation uncertainties, a multiaperture interferometric trajectory compensation algorithm is introduced and applied across the stack. Preliminary results from a single campaign day are presented, including interferometric phase and coherence stacks before and after trajectory compensation. Coherence matrices computed over three different land-cover types (cornfield, medium-height vegetation, and meadow) are analyzed as a preliminary assessment of the coherence behavior and temporal sampling capability of the HydroDrone system. Thermal and spatial decorrelation contributions are quantified to confirm that the observed coherence loss is primarily driven by temporal decorrelation, providing a robust experimental basis for future vegetation clutter decorrelation modeling.
item.authors: Pietro Grassi;Marco Manzoni;Stefano Moro;Andrea Monti-Guarnieri;Julia Kubanek;Stefano Tebaldini;

item.title: Multigranularity Selective Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models for Coastal Remote Sensing Scene Classification
item.description: Large-scale coastal reclamation activities in recent decades have had a significant impact on the sustainability of marine and terrestrial ecosystems. Remote sensing scene classification (RSSC) plays a critical role in environmental monitoring and marine management; however, existing RSSC techniques are underdeveloped for coastal regions, especially in the study of intraclass and interclass properties among different types of coastal remote sensing images. A benchmark dataset dedicated to coastal scene interpretation is crucially missing. To address this gap, we construct a new coastal remote sensing scene dataset, termed CROSS-14, which contains 3925 images spanning 14 representative coastal use patterns. To effectively handle the complex heterogeneity of coastal scenes, we propose a multigranularity selective fine-tuning (MGSF) framework to adapt vision foundation models (VFMs) for classifying coastal remote sensing images. MGSF adopts a progressive classification network consisting of linear probing and selective fine-tuning. At the sample granularity level, an uncertainty-aware reweighting (UAR) strategy is designed to emphasize difficult and ambiguous samples based on linear probing results. At the feature level, dual-selective adapters (DSA) are introduced to adaptively select informative tokens and channels while suppressing redundant representations. Extensive experiments conducted on CROSS-14 and two public benchmarks under various settings demonstrate that MGSF achieves superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/wangxinlu-y/MGSF
item.authors: Kai Zhang;Xinlu Wang;Feng Zhang;Lifeng Wang;Jiande Sun;Sen-Ching Samson Cheung;

item.title: Balancing Consistency and Generalization via Cross-Sample Memory Bank for Remote Sensing Image Change Detection
item.description: Change detection (CD) is a fundamental task in remote sensing image analysis, aiming to identify changes between images acquired at different times. For CD, it is critical to learn the consistent features of unchanged regions across multitemporal images. However, forcing consistent features also impacts the representation of diverse scenarios, resulting in decayed generalization capability. In this article, we simultaneously consider the unchanged consistency and cross-scene generalization and propose a constraint and memory network (C-MNet). First, a dual-branch backbone integrating SAM2 and VMamba is constructed to model both spatial and cross-temporal dependencies simultaneously for better capturing the consistency. Then a mask-guided dual-temporal reconstruction module is designed which enforces cross-temporal reconstruction consistency on unchanged areas and enables the network to explicitly learn temporal invariance. However, consistency-driven reconstruction tends to suppress feature diversity in different scenarios, biasing the model toward dominant land-cover patterns. To overcome this limitation, we further design a cross-sample Memory Bank mechanism that stores stable unchanged features and serves as a historical reference during training. C-MNet effectively balances consistency constraints and feature diversity, leading to improved recognition capability of changed regions and cross-scene generalization. The code of this work can be found on https://github.com/4043-lab/Change-detection
item.authors: Xia Zhang;Jinyu Han;Jia Liu;Wenhua Zhang;Fang Liu;Liang Xiao;

item.title: ReportsNet: Rotation-Enhanced Polar-Radial Topology Synergy Network for Hyperspectral and LiDAR-Derived DSM Joint Classification
item.description: Joint classification of hyperspectral (HS) imagery and light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-derived digital surface models (DSMs) commonly represents local neighborhoods on Cartesian grids, where changes in object orientation alter the spatial arrangement presented to the fusion network. Existing fusion architectures do not explicitly encode center-relative radial distances, cyclic angular relationships, or geometrically corresponding cross-modal locations. To address this gap, the rotation-enhanced polar-radial topology synergy network (ReportsNet) is proposed, which locally reorganizes co-registered HS and DSM patches into target-centered polar-radial representations and models complementary distance-based and relative-angle-aware context for multimodal fusion. On the MUUFL, Trento, and Houston datasets, ReportsNet obtains OAs of 91.99%, 99.45%, and 90.69%, respectively. It achieves the highest OA on all three datasets, exceeding the next-best compared methods by 1.44, 0.44, and 1.28 percentage points, respectively. In the Houston rotation experiment from 0° to 90°, ReportsNet yields an OA standard deviation of 0.06%, indicating stable performance under the evaluated perturbations. The code is available at https://github.com/LuyangLyu/radial-flow
item.authors: Luyang Lyu;Wenbo Yu;He Huang;Danfeng Hu;Liqiang Zhang;

item.title: Physics-Informed Causal Heterogeneous Change Detection for Geological Disaster Assessment in Steep Mountainous Terrain
item.description: Heterogeneous change detection (CD) aims to detect changes between bi-temporal remote sensing images acquired with different sensors, resolutions, and radiometric properties, a critical capability for geological disaster assessment in steep mountainous terrain. However, existing methods face three intertwined challenges: cross-sensor radiometric inconsistencies that distort feature similarity, terrain-induced pseudo-changes that mask true disaster-changed areas, and error cascades in sequential registration-then-detection pipelines. To overcome these limitations, we propose PhyCDNet, a physics-driven CD framework that fuses the interpretability of radiative transfer physics with causal inference principles. By encoding the functional structure of the radiative transfer equation as learnable network layers and explicitly applying backdoor adjustment to block terrain confounding, we bridge the gap between physical priors and causal representation learning. Our approach translates a physics-constrained optimization model into a structured network comprising a cross-resolution physical manifold alignment (CRMA) module, a physics-constrained causal orthogonal decoupling (PCOD) module, and a continuous feature-flow dynamic alignment (CFDA) module. To further eliminate registration error cascades, CFDA introduces terrain-adaptive deformation constraints, while PCOD leverages orthogonality to expedite causal disentanglement. Extensive experiments on diverse datasets demonstrate that PhyCDNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on heterogeneous steep-terrain disaster scenarios. We further validate model interpretability through post-hoc radiometric compensation quality (RCQ) and terrain decoupling index (TDI) measurements, confirming that internal feature representations conform to established physical and causal priors. By integrating physics-informed causal constraints with data-driven optimization, PhyCDNet sets a new baseline for reliable and interpretable heterogeneous CD in mountainous regions. Codes are available at our Repository.
item.authors: Zhi Li;Siying Cao;Shun Lv;Zhenming Peng;Yiguang Liu;

item.title: FMC-DETR: Frequency-Decoupled Multidomain Coordination for Aerial-View Object Detection
item.description: Remote sensing object detection (RSOD) is a critical technology for real-world applications such as natural resource monitoring, traffic management, and UAV-based rescue. Detecting tiny objects in high-resolution aerial imagery remains challenging due to weak visual cues and insufficient global context modeling in complex scenes. Existing methods often suffer from delayed contextual interaction and limited nonlinear reasoning, which restrict their ability to effectively refine shallow representations and ultimately lead to suboptimal performance. To address these challenges, we propose FMC-DETR, a frequency-decoupled fusion framework for aerial-view object detection. First, we propose the Wavelet Kolmogorov–Arnold Transformer (WeKat) backbone, which employs cascaded wavelet transforms to enhance global low-frequency structure perception in shallow features while preserving fine-grained details, and further leverages Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for adaptive nonlinear modeling of multiscale dependencies. Second, we introduce the multidomain feature coordination (MDFC) module, which refines cross-scale fused representations through partial-channel spatial, spectral, and structural coordination, thereby strengthening small-object-related feature responses in cluttered scenes. Finally, we design the compact partial fusion (CPF) module, which performs compact multibranch aggregation with progressive partial refinement to improve feature diversity and multiscale interaction while preserving stable information flow and reducing redundant perturbation. Extensive experiments across multiple remote sensing benchmarks demonstrate that FMC-DETR achieves competitive performance and consistently improves over the baseline detector. Code is available at https://github.com/bloomingvision/FMC-DETR
item.authors: Ben Liang;Hongguang Wei;Yuan Liu;Bingwen Qiu;Yihong Wang;Xiubao Sui;Qian Chen;

item.title: Intelligent Pre-Stack Common Offset Gather Denoising With Post-stack Structure Guidance
item.description: Seismic imaging is primarily used for subsurface exploration. However, the raw imaging results are often severely contaminated by various noises. To eliminate the influence of noises, various seismic denoising algorithms have been developed. Recently, deep-learning-based seismic denoising has been extensively investigated and has demonstrated significant potential. Nevertheless, most of them take only the noisy seismic image as input and directly produce the denoising output. For Pre-stack imaging gathers with extremely strong noise interference, it becomes highly challenging to discern the true structure of effective signals from the noisy input alone. This can lead denoising networks to misinterpret high-amplitude structured noise as genuine signal components, resulting in erroneous restoration. This study focuses on the Pre-stack common offset gather (COG) denoising task and proposes the prior-guided denoising (PGD) algorithm to address this challenge. The proposed PGD algorithm leverages the corresponding stacked image as a structural prior, automatically extracting guidance information to inform the denoising inference for each offset. The advantages of the proposed PGD algorithm over existing algorithms are validated through both synthetic experiments and field data applications. Field application results demonstrate that, by utilizing the stacked image as structural guidance, the PGD algorithm can restore clean single-offset images comparable in quality to Post-stack images. This not only delivers high-fidelity data for subsequent amplitude variation with offset (AVO) analysis but also enables fine-scale interpretation based on Pre-stack imaging gathers.
item.authors: Yile Ao;Wenkai Lu;Bowu Jiang;Yonghao Wang;

item.title: A Spatial–Spectral Collaborative Method for Radiometric Cross-Calibration of Ocean Color Satellite Sensors
item.description: Radiometric calibration represents an indispensable foundation for quantitative ocean color remote sensing, with cross-calibration serving as a cornerstone methodology. However, existing cross-calibration methods primarily rely on linear calibration models. These approaches struggle to accurately characterize nonlinear response residuals across complex environments and overlook both the spatial correlations among adjacent pixels and the spectral correlations between distinct bands. To address these challenges, this study departs from the conventional coefficient-fitting paradigm and proposes an innovative feature-driven radiometric cross-calibration method. By learning high-dimensional image features, this approach establishes a direct sensor-to-sensor mapping, obviating the need for explicit calibration coefficients. In particular, designed for the 3-D spatial–spectral characteristics of satellite imagery, the proposed dual-branch spatial–spectral collaborative network (DB-SSCN) synergizes local spatial features and global spectral dependencies, incorporating a band-weighted loss function to balance contributions across different bands. In a case study utilizing the Chinese Ocean Color and Temperature Scanner (COCTS) onboard the Haiyang-1-D (HY-1D) satellite, the calibration results exhibit strong consistency with the standard radiance products of Aqua MODIS, yielding a mean squared error (mse) of 0.2661 and a mean relative error (MRE) of 1.18%. Furthermore, the developed algorithm demonstrates exceptional spatial and spectral preservation capabilities, achieving a structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.9879 and a spectral angle (SA) of 0.28°. The method effectively suppresses striping artifacts, thereby significantly improving the quality of the radiometric calibration products. Application experiments confirm that the method exhibits robust applicability across diverse water environments.
item.authors: Xiaojuan Guo;Peng Ren;Yanfang Xiao;Xin Zhao;Qingjun Song;Xiaomin Ye;Keunyong Kim;Qianlong Xie;Meiyu Fan;Yi Ma;Joo-Hyung Ryu;Rongjie Liu;

item.title: Compact Multilevel-Prior Tensor Representation for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
item.description: Fusing a hyperspectral image (HSI) with a multispectral image acquired over the same scene, i.e., HSI super-resolution, has become a popular computational way to access the latent high-spatial–spectral-resolution image (HSSI). To date, a variety of fusion methods have been proposed, among which the tensor-based ones have testified that multiple priors, such as multidimensional low rankness and spatial total variation (TV) at multiple levels, effectively drive the fusion process. However, the existing tensor-based models can only effectively leverage one or two priors at one or two levels, since simultaneously incorporating multilevel priors inevitably increases model complexity. This introduces challenges in both balancing the weights of different priors and optimizing multiblock structures. Concerning this, we present a novel hyperspectral super-resolution (HSR) model compactly characterizing these multilevel priors of HSIs within the tensor framework. First, the proposed model decouples the spectral low rankness and spatial priors by casting the latent HSSI into spectral subspace and spatial maps via block term decomposition. Second, these spatial maps are stacked as the spatial tensor encoding the high-order spatial low rankness and smoothness priors, which are co-modeled via the proposed nonconvex mode-permuted tensor-correlated TV (NMP-t-CTV). Finally, we draw inspiration from the linearized alternating direction method of multipliers (LADMMs) to design an efficient algorithm to optimize the resulting model, theoretically proving its feasible-point convergence under mild conditions. Experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The code implementation is available from https://github.com/WongYinJ
item.authors: Yinjian Wang;Wei Li;Yuanyuan Gui;Gemine Vivone;

item.title: Reflected Intensity Correction Based on Global 3-D Plant Structure Acquired by Hyperspectral LiDAR
item.description: The precise quantification of 3-D plant biochemical parameters is essential for ecosystem assessment, yet acquiring accurate target reflectance remains a significant challenge for hyperspectral LiDAR (HSL) due to the strong incidence angle effect induced by complex leaf geometric morphology. Furthermore, existing correction methods are predominantly applied at a single-point scale rather than being strictly limited to it, struggling to accommodate the architectural complexity of whole plants. To address this bottleneck, this study proposes a novel reflectance correction framework for HSL based on the global 3-D structural information of the entire plant to suppress the effects of incidence angle on reflectance. Methodologically, an adaptive neighborhood point determination method based on point density is designed to accurately compute leaf curvature and normal vectors from point clouds, thereby avoiding over-smoothing or geometric distortion. Subsequently, a physically improved Cook–Torrance model for HSL (HSL-CT) is established to decouple diffuse and specular reflectance contributions across 28 spectral bands ranging from 445 to 810 nm. The evaluation results demonstrate that the proposed HSL-CT model consistently outperforms the baseline Lambert–Beckmann (LB) model in overall fitting accuracy and spectral fidelity. By integrating this model with the extracted global structural information, the framework effectively eliminates angular-induced specular over-brightness, significantly reduces spectral errors, and successfully restores native plant spectral signatures. Ultimately, this method can generate incidence-angle-corrected HSL reflectance data with high stability, laying a solid foundation for accurate inversion of biochemical parameters at the individual plant scale.
item.authors: Ao Wang;Shuo Shi;Binhan Luo;Qian Xu;Xingtao Tang;Jian Yang;Ximing Ren;Chengyu Gong;Wei Gong;

item.title: ASG-SAM: Anisotropic Spectral Gating and Multigranularity Decoding for SAM-Based Infrared Small Target Segmentation
item.description: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) remains challenging due to the extremely small spatial support, weak texture, low target-background contrast, and severe clutter interference. Although the Segment Anything Model (SAM) provides strong promptable segmentation ability, its direct adaptation to IRSTD is still limited. Generic Cartesian feature aggregation is not well matched to the point-spread characteristics of infrared small targets, while fragile target cues are easily diluted during deep semantic propagation. To address these issues, this article proposes anisotropic spectral gating (ASG)-SAM, a physics-aware SAM adaptation framework for infrared small target segmentation. In particular, an ASG module is introduced as a joint radial-angular spectral gate parameterized in the polar frequency domain, improving the compatibility between feature aggregation and point-spread target characteristics. In addition, a difference-of-Gaussians adaptive multigranularity decoder (DoG-AMGD) is designed to recycle intermediate vision transformer (ViT) features and adaptively fuse difference-of-Gaussian (DoG)-style differential cues across multiple granularities, thereby recovering high-frequency target details while suppressing clutter-induced responses. Extensive experiments on three public IRSTD benchmarks, including IRSTD-1K, NUAA-SIRST, and IRSTDID-SKY, demonstrate that ASG-SAM achieves state-of-the-art segmentation performance. Moreover, applying ASG to different SAM variants consistently brings substantial improvements, showing its general effectiveness for adapting promptable segmentation models to infrared small target scenarios. Ablation studies and feature visualizations further verify the complementary effectiveness and interpretability of ASG and DoG-AMGD.
item.authors: Riyao Chen;Mingchao Yang;Zehao Wu;Tianming Xie;Wenxiong Kang;

item.title: A Novel Physics-Based Empirical Line Approach for Reflectance Calibration of UAV Multispectral Imagery
item.description: Accurate reflectance estimation from uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery is critical for a wide range of applications and is achieved using various calibration methods. The conventional empirical line method (ELM) is a statistical digital number (DN) calibration approach that ignores input irradiance, which can introduce reflectance errors, whereas more physically accurate approaches require additional upward-looking irradiance sensors and separate calibration procedures. This study presents a novel reflectance formulation that bridges physical reflectance modeling and statistical DN calibration by reconstructing effective irradiance directly from reference panels, eliminating the need for an irradiance sensor. The method does not require additional irradiance sensors on the UAV or ground and was evaluated under variable illumination conditions. The proposed workflow first extracts raw DNs from UAV multispectral imagery together with four ground reference panels of known reflectance to establish the physical relationship between surface reflectance, radiance, and irradiance. The reference panels are measured at the start or end of the flight, or during UAV overpass acquisition. The certified spectral library of the reference calibration panels provides physically reliable reference reflectance values, which are incorporated into the radiometric model to reconstruct the effective irradiance and preserve the physical irradiance–reflectance relationship throughout the calibration process. Finally, the calibration coefficients are solved using a weighted least-squares optimization to estimate the effective irradiance. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves reflectance accuracy ( $R^{2}=0.96$ ) and robustness compared with the conventional ELM. The proposed method reduced the root mean square error (RMSE) by approximately 50% compared with the conventional ELM approach. Overall, the proposed method offers a practical calibration approach for UAV-based reflectance estimation without requiring an additional irradiance sensor.
item.authors: Davoud Ashourloo;Daniel Smith;Lleyton Cave;Chris James;Xiaolong Chen;Sebastian Lopez-Marcano;Riku Oya;Carla Gho Brito;Andries B. Potgieter;Scott Chapman;

item.title: G-SIR: Gaussian Semantic Inverse Rendering for Scaling Open-Vocabulary 3-D Understanding to City-Scale Scenes
item.description: Integrating open-vocabulary semantics into explicit 3-D representations is essential for embodied agents to interpret unseen concepts, yet scaling such representations to city-scale scenes remains challenging. The dominant neural distillation paradigm suffers from neural spectral bias, which suppresses high-frequency semantic boundaries, and costly iterative optimization over large 3-D representations. We present Gaussian semantic inverse rendering (G-SIR), which recasts semantic lifting as a constrained inverse problem with analytical tractability. Built on surface-aligned 2-D Gaussian splatting (2DGS), G-SIR comprises four sequential stages: 1) geometry-informed feature lifting (G-LIFT) extracts dense CLIP-based semantic supervision; 2) Anchor-based projection with manifold optimization (AP-MO) formulates a similarity-preserving projection using scene-specific text anchors; 3) R-SIR iteratively optimizes the projection on the Stiefel manifold; and 4) closed-form solving performs regularized per-Gaussian semantic assignment without iterative semantic-field optimization. This formulation avoids iterative per-Gaussian neural semantic fitting while improving semantic boundary fidelity. On LERF-Mask, G-SIR achieves the best mean intersection over union (mIoU) and mean boundary IoU (mBIoU) across all three evaluated scenes. On MatrixCity and UrbanScene3D, where pixel-level semantic ground truth is unavailable, experiments provide qualitative semantic evidence together with quantitative efficiency evaluation. UrbanScene3D further provides qualitative evidence of cross-scene semantic generalization across related scenes under scene-specific fitting. G-SIR completes semantic embedding in 15 and 40 min on MatrixCity and UrbanScene3D, respectively, demonstrating practical scalability to city-scale scenes.

item.title: PST-DUNet: A Progressive Spectral Topology-Aware Deep Unfolding Network for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution
item.description: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) contain rich spectral fingerprints. However, restricted by hardware bottlenecks, the acquired images often fail to satisfy the requirements for fine-grained observation. Although HSI super-resolution has achieved significant progress, many existing methods still primarily emphasize spatial detail recovery and exploit cross-band information through implicit feature interactions or output-level spectral constraints. Such a spatial-first reconstruction paradigm may provide insufficient cross-band coordination during progressive detail generation, leading to inconsistent interband response patterns and spectral distortion. To address this issue, we propose a progressive spectral topology-aware deep unfolding network (PST-DUNet). In particular, we adopt a progressive low-resolution (LR)–mid resolution (MR)–high-resolution (HR) reconstruction strategy to reduce the difficulty of direct large-scale reconstruction. In the MR stage, a parameterized observation-consistency correction is introduced to constrain the intermediate estimate with the LR observation. Meanwhile, we design an instance-adaptive dynamic spectral topology inference (DSTI) module to infer reconstruction-state-conditioned interband dependencies. Furthermore, a spectral topology rectifier (STR) is introduced to transform the topology-aggregated spectral representation into channelwise gating coefficients, thereby modulating spatial feature updates and alleviating spectral distortion. Extensive experiments on the evaluated public HSI datasets like Pavia Center, Chikusei, and CAVE demonstrate that PST-DUNet achieves superior reconstruction performance under the nonblind degradation setting, providing a favorable balance between spatial detail recovery and spectral consistency preservation.
item.authors: Zhenyu Li;Xiangrong Zhang;Guanchun Wang;Huiyu Zhou;Xiao Han;Licheng Jiao;

item.title: Physically Constrained Machine Learning Retrieval of Turbulence Dissipation Rate From Radar Wind Profiler
item.description: Atmospheric turbulence dissipation rate ( $\varepsilon $ ) is a key parameter for understanding boundary-layer turbulence and its impacts on atmospheric processes. Machine learning (ML) techniques have been applied to retrieve $\varepsilon $ from radar wind profiler (RWP) observations, but their inherently data-driven nature and strong dependence on turbulent samples lead to overestimation under weak-turbulence conditions, limiting their operational applicability. To address this limitation, this study proposes a physically constrained random forest (RF) framework for retrieving $\varepsilon $ from RWP observations. The method integrates physical knowledge of boundary-layer turbulence into the RF retrieval through a two-step correction strategy, consisting of a boundary constraint to suppress physically implausible estimates under weak turbulence and an empirical scaling adjustment to enhance sensitivity in low turbulence regimes. The proposed approach is evaluated using one year of the RWP and sonic anemometer measurements at 160 and 320 m at the Shenzhen Shiyan site in Southern China. Results show that the proposed correction improves retrieval performance, increasing the correlation coefficient with in situ measurements from 0.67 to 0.78 and reducing the mean absolute error (MAE) across different turbulence intensities, atmospheric conditions, and seasons. The corrected retrievals reproduce realistic diurnal variations of $\varepsilon $ , with enhanced daytime turbulence and higher values under clear-sky conditions compared with cloudy periods. These findings provide an effective approach for estimating $\varepsilon $ from RWP observations, and support the use of RWP for long-term and operational investigations of boundary-layer turbulence.
